Factor by Grouping Algebra 3/4 · Notes p. 60–61

Algebra 3/4 · Factoring

Factor by Grouping

A way to factor polynomials that have four terms. Have your notebook open to pages 60–61.

2x2 + 8x + 3x + 12  ⟶  (x + 4)(2x + 3)

Auto-run plays the lesson like a video. Step by step lets you press Next. Switch between them anytime at the bottom. Just want to copy? Press Show all steps. Captions & view moves or enlarges the captions.

Page 60 · Let's look at an example

2x2 + 8x + 3x + 12

Do all 4 terms share a common GCF?

2x22 · 1
8x2 · 2 · 2
3x3 · 1
122 · 2 · 3
ONLY 1
Why?

3 doesn't have a factor of 2, and 12 has no x. A GCF of 1 doesn't help, so we need a new plan.

Page 60

Notice what happens when we split it in half

2x2 + 8xsplit+ 3x + 12
GCF = 2x split GCF = 3
Hint

2 and 8 both divide by 2, and both terms have at least one x.

Page 60

Let's factor those out… What do you notice?

2x2 ÷ 2x = x    8x ÷ 2x = 4   2x(x + 4)
3x ÷ 3 = x    12 ÷ 3 = 4   3(x + 4)
2x(x + 4) + 3(x + 4)
Same! Both parentheses are (x + 4).

Page 60

Now factor the common binomial out

2x(x + 4) + 3(x + 4)

Think of (x + 4) as one chunk. How many chunks do we have? 2x · x + 4  +  3 · x + 4  =  (2x + 3) · x + 4

Like 2 apples + 3 apples = 5 apples. The leftovers (underlined) group together into their own parentheses.

(x + 4)(2x + 3)
Completely factored :)
Check

Multiply back: (x + 4)(2x + 3) = 2x² + 3x + 8x + 12. It matches. Either order is fine: (2x + 3)(x + 4) is the same answer.

Page 61

Factor by Grouping: the steps

  • Steps: When you have 4 terms:
  • 1.Split your polynomial down the middle
  • 2.Find the GCF of each half.
  • 3.Factor out each side's GCF.
  • 4.Factor out the common binomial.

Page 61 · Example 1 · Factor completely

3x2 − 6x + 4x − 8

3x2 − 6xsplit+ 4x − 8
GCF = 3xsplitGCF = 4
3x(x − 2) + 4(x − 2)
(x − 2)(3x + 4)

Page 61 · Example 2 · Factor completely

2y3 + 20y2 + y + 10

2y3 + 20y2split+ y + 10
GCF = 2y2splitGCF = 1
Watch outOnly GCF is 1? Factor out 1.
2y2(y + 10) + 1(y + 10)
(y + 10)(2y2 + 1)

Page 61 · Example 3 · Factor completely

5y3 − 30y2 − y + 6

5y3 − 30y2split− y + 6
GCF = 5y2splitGCF = −1
Watch outHalf starts negative? Factor out a negative GCF (here −1; could be −3, −5…).
5y2(y − 6) − 1(y − 6)
Signs flip

Factoring out the negative flipped the signs inside: − y + 6 became −1(y − 6).

(y − 6)(5y2 − 1)

Review

Three things to watch for

1

GCF is 1? Write the 1. It becomes the "+ 1" in your answer.

2

Second half starts negative? Factor out a negative GCF, then check both signs.

3

Binomials don't match? Recheck your GCFs and signs. They have to match before step 4.

Wrap-up

You've got it

  1. Split the polynomial down the middle.
  2. Find the GCF of each half. 1 or −1 counts
  3. Factor out each side's GCF. The binomials should match.
  4. Factor out the common binomial. done

Check any answer by multiplying it back out.

Optional

Practice on your own

Six problems. For each one:

  1. Work it in your notebook first.
  2. Stuck? Open Hint 1 (the GCFs), then Hint 2 (the factored-out form).
  3. Pick your answer to check it. Wrong answers tell you what to fix.

Practice 1 of 6 Optional

x2 + 5x + 2x + 10

Hint 1 · Split + GCFs
x² + 5x → GCF = xsplit+ 2x + 10 → GCF = 2
Hint 2 · Factor out each GCF
x(x + 5) + 2(x + 5)
Solution
(x + 5)(x + 2)

Practice 2 of 6 Optional

6x2 + 9x + 4x + 6

Hint 1 · Split + GCFs
6x² + 9x → GCF = 3xsplit+ 4x + 6 → GCF = 2
Hint 2 · Factor out each GCF
3x(2x + 3) + 2(2x + 3)
Solution
(2x + 3)(3x + 2)

Practice 3 of 6 Optional

x3 + 4x2 + 3x + 12

Hint 1 · Split + GCFs
x³ + 4x² → GCF = x²split+ 3x + 12 → GCF = 3
Hint 2 · Factor out each GCF
x²(x + 4) + 3(x + 4)
Solution
(x + 4)(x² + 3)

Practice 4 of 6 Optional

2x3 − 8x2 + x − 4

Hint 1 · Split + GCFs
2x³ − 8x² → GCF = 2x²split+ x − 4 → GCF = 1
Hint 2 · Factor out each GCF
2x²(x − 4) + 1(x − 4)
Solution
(x − 4)(2x² + 1)

Practice 5 of 6 Optional

3y3 + 12y2 − y − 4

Hint 1 · Split + GCFs
3y³ + 12y² → GCF = 3y²split− y − 4 → GCF = −1
Hint 2 · Factor out each GCF
3y²(y + 4) − 1(y + 4)
Solution
(y + 4)(3y² − 1)

Practice 6 of 6 Optional

4x3 − 20x2 − 3x + 15

Hint 1 · Split + GCFs
4x³ − 20x² → GCF = 4x²split− 3x + 15 → GCF = −3
Hint 2 · Factor out each GCF
4x²(x − 5) − 3(x − 5)
Solution
(x − 5)(4x² − 3)
